chunk.line: To enable it: set splittable=true and a min_chunk_minutes on that operation's routing line in routing_lines.csv (the run phase becomes resumable; chunk boundaries fall on calendar boundaries, and nothing is billed to the pause). See the incoming-data spec §5.3.

window.line: Yes — extra working hours beyond the regular shift — an overtime window a job can run in when the regular calendar is closed, priced at a premium so the schedule only buys those hours when they pay for themselves (e.g. a Saturday shift that rescues a tight order).

bound.line: Proving optimality requires not just finding a good solution but also a matching lower bound; many scheduling objectives (like total tardiness or weighted lateness) give lower bounds that are weak or slow to compute, so the gap between the best found solution and the best provable bound can stay open for a long time. makespan.line: The lower bound side of the gap is often weak for scheduling objectives like tardiness or makespan, because relaxations (dropping integrality or precedence) can be far looser than the real problem — so a stubbornly large reported gap can mean the bound is poor rather than that the incumbent schedule is actually far from optimal.
